subject.title: Gateway leaks transient sessions when target session transcript is missing during polling

question: When `/tools/invoke` `sessions_list` targets a session whose transcript file is missing, should Gateway return a non-mutating not-found/empty result, recreate a single explicit placeholder, or defer to doctor/cleanup repair?
rationale: The issue proposes several acceptable behaviors, and root policy treats runtime fallbacks and state repair as product choices rather than implementation conveniences.

options.title: Prefer non-mutating read behavior
options.body: Return a clear not-found, empty, or warning-shaped result without creating or persisting a new session during polling.

options.title: Self-heal once with an explicit owner
options.body: Create one placeholder or repair record only through a named session/doctor owner path with regression proof that repeated polling does not churn state.

options.title: Defer until live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open for current-main live reproduction before choosing the API behavior or fix boundary.

recommendation.title: Prefer non-mutating read behavior
recommendation.body: Return a clear not-found, empty, or warning-shaped result without creating or persisting a new session during polling.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent session-store/tooling history make this the best available routing candidate for the Gateway/session-state product choice.
